title: Gateway Security
description: Learn to secure API Gateways and protect microservices from common attacks.

data.text: The API Gateway is the security perimeter of your microservices architecture. Amazon, Google, and Stripe all treat their API Gateway as the first line of defense, implementing authentication, authorization, and threat protection before requests reach internal services.

data.title: Security at the Gateway
items: TLS termination: Encrypt traffic in transit
Authentication: Verify client identity (OAuth2, JWT, API keys)
Threat protection: WAF rules to block SQL injection, XSS, etc.
Rate limiting: Prevent abuse and DoS attacks
IP allowlisting: Restrict access to known IPs for internal APIs

data.text: The gateway should validate authentication tokens before forwarding requests. This offloads auth logic from internal services and ensures that only authenticated requests reach your microservices. Pass the user identity in headers like X-User-ID or X-Email.

data.title: Never Trust the Client
data.text: Always validate tokens at the gateway, even if internal services also validate. Defense in depth means multiple layers of security.

data.title: Example: Gateway Authentication Plugin
data.code:
# Kong JWT plugin configuration
plugins:
  - name: jwt
    service: user-service
    config:
      claims_to_verify:
        - exp
      key_claim_name: iss
      secrets_are_base64: false

# After validation, Kong adds headers:
# X-User-ID: user-123
# X-User-Email: alice@example.com

data.caption: Security layers at the API Gateway
data.definition:
graph LR
    C[Client] --> G[API Gateway]
    G -->|1. TLS| T[TLS Termination]
    T -->|2. Auth| A[Auth Check]
    A -->|3. WAF| W[WAF Rules]
    W -->|4. Rate Limit| RL[Rate Limiter]
    RL -->|5. Forward| S[Backend Service]

items.question: Should internal services validate auth too?
items.answer: Yes. Gateway auth is the first line; services should validate for critical operations. Use mTLS for service-to-service auth.

items.question: What is a WAF?
items.answer: A Web Application Firewall (WAF) inspects incoming traffic for common attacks like SQL injection, XSS, and CSRF. AWS WAF, Cloudflare, and ModSecurity are popular implementations.

items.question: How do I handle DDoS protection?
items.answer: Use cloud DDoS protection (AWS Shield, Cloudflare) at the edge. Rate limiting at the gateway provides additional protection.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Gateway is the security perimeter of microservices
Validate auth at the gateway to offload internal services
Use WAF for common attack protection
Apply defense in depth with multiple security layers
data.takeaway: Secure the API Gateway first; it is the most exposed component of your microservices architecture.
